external_entities.name: Duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who opens the dispatch console in a browser.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

external_entities.name: Scheduling partner
external_entities.description: An external scheduling partner that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: Dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application opened by duty engineers in a browser and used to call the dispatch API and maintain a WebSocket for live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it. The console and the API are served from different origins.

processes.name: Corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: Dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: Schedule importer
processes.description: A process on the corporate network that pulls and parses the partner's SOAP feed, archives downloaded XML documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: It presents an API token to the dispatch API. The token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

data_stores.name: Dispatch database
data_stores.description: The database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order in it carries the token or the session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: Schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder on the corporate file store containing each XML document downloaded from the scheduling partner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: serve application
data_flows.description: A duty engineer loads the dispatch application from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and the API are served from different origins. Whoever configured CORS did not record which origins the API allows, or whether it allows credentials.
data_flows.data_description: Dispatch console API requests and responses

data_flows.name: stream job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether that socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: Job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS every hour.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies our importer, or how our importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: Tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write document
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded XML document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: It presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers and the schedule importer run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: Production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company, same-staff zone holding the live estate, with authority to move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of those rights. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: Scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: A zone controlled by the separate company that operates the scheduling partner.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API presents a web interface because the console communicates with it cross-origin and its CORS configuration is described.
assumptions.basis: The description says the console and API are served from different origins and that the API answers the console cross-origin using CORS.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch importer presents a non-web interface because it is described as a batch importer that periodically pulls, parses, archives, and posts data.
assumptions.basis: The importer runs hourly and performs batch feed-processing behavior rather than presenting a caller-programmed web application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database contains confidential data because it holds personal contact information and tokens or sessions.
assumptions.basis: The database holds crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
